questions.q:
What is the primary role of a bank in an economy?
(Recall: Simple direct question)
questions.a: The bank acts as an intermediary that takes money from depositors and lends it to people or businesses who need it for productive activities. A wrong answer suggests the bank is just a safe or a locker, missing the concept of money circulation and economic activity.

questions.q:
Why is it said that banks are like the "circulatory system" of the economy?
(Understand: Explaining the metaphor)
questions.a: Just as blood carries nutrients to all parts of the body to keep it alive, banks carry money to all parts of the economy to keep it productive. A wrong answer shows the student thinks money stays inside the bank rather than flowing out to businesses and individuals.

questions.q:
If a student takes a loan from a bank to pay for their education, how does this fit into the bank's role?
(Apply: Using the concept in a new scenario)
questions.a: The bank provides the capital (loan) so the student can gain skills, which will eventually allow them to do productive work and contribute to the economy. A wrong answer suggests that loans are only for businesses, ignoring that education is an investment in human capital.

questions.q:
Compare a bank's role to a treasure chest that locks away gold coins. How are they different?
(Analyze: Comparing and contrasting)
questions.a: A treasure chest keeps wealth "idle," meaning it cannot be used by anyone else to create value. A bank, however, keeps money "active" by lending it out to fuel growth, showing that money in a bank contributes to the economy while money in a chest does not.

questions.q:
Is a bank that keeps all its money in a vault and refuses to give loans truly part of the economy? Why or why not?
(Evaluate: Judging the concept)
questions.a: No, because that bank is not circulating money; it is acting like a storage locker. For a bank to support the economy, it must move money from savers to borrowers to create "value addition" (like a farmer buying seeds or a carpenter buying wood).

questions.q:
Imagine a town with no banks. What would happen to someone who wants to start a small shop but has no savings?
(Create: Scenario generation)
questions.a: The shopkeeper would be unable to borrow, their idea would not happen, and the economy would grow much slower. A good answer identifies that without banks, money gets "trapped" with the wealthy and cannot reach the people who have the skills to build new things.

questions.q: Fill in the blank: Banks are financial ______ that act as a bridge by collecting money from people who have extra savings and lending it to those who need capital for productive activities.
Fill in the blank: Have you ever wondered what happens to the money your parents put in a ______ account?
What is Banks? State the definition given in this lesson.
questions.a: Banks are financial institutions that act as a bridge by collecting money from people who have extra savings and lending it to those who need capital for productive activities.

questions.q: What common mix-up does this lesson flag about Banks?
questions.a: Students often believe that banks keep every customer's money in a separate personal drawer in the back.

questions.q: What must you be able to do to master this topic?
questions.a: The student must be able to explain that a bank is not just a storage box for money, but a tool that turns idle savings into active investments like loans for businesses or farmers.
